title: John Brinkley: The Quackiest Quack in History?
summary: Josh and Chuck profile John R. Brinkley, the Kansas-based "quack" who in the 1920s and 1930s built a fortune performing fake goat gland transplant surgeries. The episode opens with a listener shout-out (Matt Sinofsky, Austin) and a background on xeno-transplantation, from early blood transfusions from animals and animal skin grafts through Brown-Sequard's testicle serum and Voronoff's monkey gland surgeries. It then covers Brinkley's birth in North Carolina, his medicine-show days, his eclectic medical training, his move to Milford, Kansas, and the goat gland procedure, which was really a slice of goat testicle inserted into the scrotum. It describes his publicity (the Harry Chandler/LA Times endorsement), his Kansas radio station KFKB and the Medical Question Box, the AMA's Morris Fishbein and the Kansas Medical Board revoking his license, his 1930 write-in run for Kansas governor, his move to Mexico and the powerful XERA border radio station, his prostate "Formula 10-20" treatment, the libel suit against Fishbein in which he admitted the surgery didn't work, his losses and death in 1942 before a mail fraud trial. The episode closes with a listener email about Lula Naff and the Ryman Theatre, and ad reads appear at the start and in breaks.

segments.title: Xenotransplantation history
segments.summary: Definition of xenotransplantation and early history, including Jean-Baptiste Denis's animal blood transfusions in 1600s France, 19th century animal skin grafts, and the belief that animal glands could restore vigor.

segments.title: Glandular rejuvenation and early physicians
segments.summary: Ancient beliefs about eating animal parts for virility, Brown-Sequard's testicle serum experiments, and Voronoff's monkey testicle and chimpanzee thyroid surgeries in Paris, which inspired the monkey gland cocktail.

segments.title: Brinkley's early life and medicine show
segments.summary: Brinkley's birth in North Carolina in 1885, his family arrangement, his early medicine show work with his first wife, and his interest in quackery.

segments.title: Eclectic medical school and Milford, Kansas
segments.summary: Brinkley's training at Bennett Medical College, the Flexner Report's impact on eclectic medicine, his practice in Milford, Kansas, and the farmer who requested the first goat gland procedure.
